title: United wins Portimão as G-Drive loses podium to penalty
dek: Phil Hanson and Filipe Albuquerque won the ELMS finale for United from third on the grid, 0.520 seconds ahead of Panis Barthez, after a 10-second penalty cost champions G-Drive the podium.

chapters.title: Nothing left to win, plenty left to fight for
text: The 4 Hours of Portimão on 28 October 2018 closed the European Le Mans Series season with the LMP2 title already settled. G-Drive Racing's Oreca #26 had been crowned at Spa, where the rain-shortened race paid only half points, so the class arrived at the Algarve International Circuit with nothing left to decide at the top. What remained was the scrap behind. Racing Engineering and IDEC Sport came in level on 56 points, with DragonSpeed six back on 50. Racing Engineering had won on its debut at Le Castellet but scored only three points across Silverstone and Spa combined, IDEC's #28 Oreca had finished every race, and DragonSpeed had taken second place at both Silverstone and Spa.

The entry numbered 39 cars, 15 of them in LMP2. IDEC Sport was again without its full-season sister car, absent for the second time that year, and Paul Lafargue was still out with serious back problems, so Gabriel Aubry joined Paul Loup Chatin and Memo Rojas in the #28 for a second race. Lafargue underwent surgery during the weekend. United Autosports arrived with confidence, having switched to Michelin tyres from Spa and tested at the circuit the previous Wednesday. Nicolas Lapierre, racing the DragonSpeed #21 that weekend, was named on Saturday as the lead driver of Cool Racing's new LMP2 programme for 2019, and the team's fresh Oreca was already sitting in the paddock.

Practice gave little away. Nicolas Jamin put the Duqueine Engineering Oreca #29 on top of dry Friday morning running with a 1:32.846, the United Ligiers within a quarter of a second, before a heavy downpour hit that afternoon. On a cooler, breezier Saturday morning Chatin topped the second session for IDEC on 1:33.097, heading an Oreca 1-2-3 ahead of DragonSpeed and G-Drive.

chapters.title: Jamin snatches pole on the final lap
text: Duqueine Engineering took its first LMP2 pole in dramatic fashion. Jamin had spent more than seven minutes in the pits, then went out and set 1:33.197 on his last flying lap to take pole in the #29 Oreca, the first ELMS pole of his career and a first for the team in its debut season in the class. Will Stevens had thought he had pole for Panis Barthez Competition when he crossed the line just after the flag with 1:33.257, but the Ligier #23 ended 0.060 seconds short. His team-mate Pierre Ragues said the objective was to fight for the podium and possibly for the win.

Filipe Albuquerque had held top spot until the final flurry and had to settle for third in the United Autosports Ligier #22 on 1:33.363, giving him a home-race start from the second row. Chatin put the IDEC Oreca fourth on 1:33.652, with the G-Drive Oreca #26 fifth on 1:33.836 and Lapierre's DragonSpeed sixth. The sister United car of Will Owen was seventh and the AVF by Adrián Vallés Dallara #30 of Henrique Chaves the best of the Dallaras in eighth.

The title chasers were scattered. Racing Engineering's Olivier Pla could manage only 1:34.634 for 12th, behind Felipe Nasr's Cetilar Villorba Corse Dallara in ninth and the second G-Drive Oreca in tenth, leaving the Spanish team with work to do. Race start was set for 12:30 local time.

chapters.title: Duqueine leads, United waits
text: Phil Hanson started the #22 Ligier from third and spent the opening stint stuck in traffic, catching slower cars at exactly the wrong places. Ragues drove the opening stint in the pole-sitting Duqueine and led the early running, while the two cars ahead of Hanson were locking up under braking in their own duel, with tyre smoke rising at the corners. Hanson's approach was to save his tyres, often taking just a single new one at pit stops, and to hold the gap while the cars in front used theirs up.
Only 39 cars were sharing a track under three miles long, and traffic shaped everyone's lap times from the first lap.

chapters.title: Duqueine breaks, Nasr leads
text: The Duqueine's challenge ended after just 52 laps when a suspension problem stopped it, and the #29 was not classified. A Full Course Yellow came around the halfway mark. Nasr, meanwhile, charged from ninth on the grid through the top ten to the front in the Cetilar Villorba Corse Dallara #47. He then lost ground after being handed a drive-through for a near-miss with a GTE car, and the Dallara finished 24th, eleven laps down.
DragonSpeed had a day to forget. Its #21 Oreca, in which Lapierre set the fastest lap of the race at 1:35.078, finished 35th, 40 laps down. The AVF Dallara #30 was not classified after 68 laps.

chapters.title: A Safety Car resets the lead fight
text: A Safety Car in the final hour bunched the field and turned a spread-out afternoon into a four-way fight for the lead between the United Ligiers #22 and #32, the Panis Barthez Ligier #23 and the G-Drive Oreca #26. The title-winning Oreca was at the centre of it until Jean-Eric Vergne was penalised for running off the road while passing a GTE car at the height of the battle. The penalty was 10 seconds, to be added to the car's finishing time.

chapters.title: Half a second, then a penalty bites
text: Albuquerque took the car to the flag and held off Stevens by 0.520 seconds after 140 laps. Stevens, sharing the Panis Barthez car with Julien Canal and Timothé Buret, had risen from fourth to second in the closing stint, passing Owen in the sister United car and then Andrea Pizzitola's G-Drive Oreca, and spent the last laps pressing the leader. Albuquerque said afterwards that he had managed the tyres and traffic well but suffered oversteer that made it hard to stay in front.

On the road the G-Drive Oreca had crossed the line about five seconds behind the winner, but with Vergne's 10-second penalty added the car dropped to fourth, 0.538 seconds behind Owen's United Ligier. That handed the final podium place to Owen, Hugo de Sadeleer and Wayne Boyd, and made it a Ligier 1-2-3 on Michelin tyres. Racing Engineering was fifth, ahead of IDEC Sport's #28 in sixth, with the second G-Drive Oreca and the Graff Oreca seventh and eighth.

chapters.title: Back-to-back wins and a tight fight for second
text: It was a second consecutive win for the United pair and, for Hanson, a more satisfying one than Spa, where the race was stopped early. He called it the hardest, almost quadruple stint of his career, said he had asked his engineer more than once how long remained, and credited Albuquerque with coaching him in tyre saving all season. Albuquerque simply said it was two in a row now. Panis Barthez Competition, which had pushed so hard through the closing laps, left slightly disappointed with second.

For G-Drive Racing the afternoon brought a lost podium but not a lost season. Roman Rusinov and Pizzitola finished the year with 100.25 points as drivers' champions, and the team's Oreca finished 34.25 points clear of Racing Engineering. Vergne, who missed Le Castellet, finished on 88.25. The title carries an entry to the 2019 24 Hours of Le Mans for G-Drive.

The race for second in the championship went to the Spanish team. Racing Engineering's fifth place with Norman Nato, Pla and Paul Petit lifted it from 56 to 66 points, two clear of IDEC Sport, which gained eight with sixth to finish on 64. United Autosports ended fourth on 54 points after a season Hanson described as up and down, while DragonSpeed took fifth on just over 50. Racing Engineering was named Team of the Year at the closing ceremony. Duqueine Engineering, eighth in the teams standings on 35 points after its first LMP2 season, said it wanted a full ELMS campaign and a Le Mans entry in 2019.

The 2019 grid began to take shape immediately. Several teams stayed in Portugal for a test on Monday to Wednesday, among them Cool Racing and RLR MSport with new Orecas, and Hanson and Albuquerque were confirmed to stay at United for another year in a Ligier. The next European Le Mans Series season begins at Paul Ricard in April 2019.

facts.v: Jamin set 1:33.197 on his final lap, 0.060 seconds ahead of Stevens, to take Duqueine Engineering's first LMP2 pole.
